title: Pool Forge — Node-level Health Mosaic & Autoscale Handoff Prototype
creator: Priya Nair
description: Objective: Design a compact console panel that surfaces node-level health signals for a Dedicated GPU pool and provides a clear handoff for autoscale/ burst decisions. The panel (Pool Forge) should let operators quickly identify problematic nodes, see thermal and utilization mosaics, understand cost implications of burst decisions, and trigger a safe autoscale handoff to infra. Scope: 1) Node health mosaic (mini sparkline + status overlays), 2) Burst intent composer (budget-aware, canary toggles, optional thermal-safety guard), 3) Autoscale handoff card (preflight checks and suggested instance types), 4) Cost lens that shows token-cost delta for burst windows. Out of scope: multi-region routing changes, RBAC policy authoring, and rollout orchestration (handled by PM/Eng tickets). Constraints: must render in console sidecar with limited vertical space (300–420px), align with Console V2 color tokens and accessibility (WCAG AA), and be wireframe-friendly for rapid A/B testing with operators.
acceptance_criteria: Design artifact (Figma) includes node mosaic, burst composer, autoscale handoff card, and cost lens with responsive variants for compact and expanded panel
Prototype shows primary flows: identify unhealthy node -> compose burst -> preview cost delta -> trigger autoscale handoff
Design annotated with accessibility notes (contrast ratios, keyboard focus order, ARIA labels) and documented microcopy for risk states
Eng review signoff: layout fits 320–420px height container and components map to existing Console token and component library
Usability validation: 3 operator interviews with positive completion for core flow (identify + trigger)
comments: 2025-02-18 Priya Nair: Kickoff — aligned with PM on goals. Noted requirement to surface both thermal and KV-cache pressure signals. Asked Eng for API field list by 02/21.

2025-02-21 Diego Martinez (Eng): Provided initial telemetry fields: node_id, gpu_temp_c, util_gpu_pct, util_mem_pct, avg_latency_ms, kv_cache_miss_rate, recent_restarts. Also recommended limiting refresh to 5s for the compact view.

2025-02-24 Liam O'Connor: Shared first high-fidelity mosaic variants. Trade-off discussed: showing sparkline for GPU temp vs showing current temp badge. Decided to prioritize sparkline for trend plus color band for current state.

2025-02-25 PM review (Ava Chen): Requested cost lens to include estimated token cost per burst minute and a 'budget slider' for quick presets (Low/Medium/High). Also flagged need for 'safe mode' to guard against thermal spikes.

2025-02-27 Design critique: Feedback from Design Guild — simplify burst composer to three fields (preset slider, canary % of pool, duration). Remove free-form JSON editor from primary flow and move to advanced modal.

2025-03-01 Eng sync (Jordan Kim): Raised concern about autoscale handoff requiring preflight checks; suggested adding a 'dry-run' preview showing expected instance allocation and expected SLO impact. Added ENG-50123 to implement preflight API.

2025-03-02 Usability test (prototype v0.2) — 3 operators: all could identify an overheating node; 2/3 initially misinterpreted the canary % UI; updated microcopy and tooltip to clarify 'canary % of pool capacity'
2025-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Updated Figma to v0.3. Ready for formal design review with Eng + PM on 2025-03-05. Included annotated component mapping for frontend (tokens + CSS classes).
notes: Decision log: Use a compact mosaic grid (3 cols) with color-coded status: green (healthy), amber (degraded), red (critical). Hover reveals last 1h sparkline and key metrics.
Trade-offs: We opted to limit visible metrics to reduce cognitive load; advanced metrics available in drill-in modal.
Follow-ups: PM to schedule rollout gating criteria with SRE; Eng to expose preflight API by 2025-03-07; Design to produce microcopy for all states by 2025-03-04.
